assumptions.choice: Use a minimal price-comparison rule as the unstated 'core strategy' signal: enter long when close[0] > close[-1], exit when close[0] < close[-1]; not a named technical indicator.
assumptions.reason: The spec delegates buy/sell signal generation to an external, unspecified core trading system and explicitly states no indicators are used; a minimal literal comparison isolates the exchange-schedule filter that is the actual subject of the spec.

assumptions.choice: Compute NYSE/NASDAQ full-closure holidays algorithmically (New Year's Day, MLK Day, Presidents Day, Good Friday via the Meeus/Jones/Butcher Easter algorithm, Memorial Day, Juneteenth from 2022 onward, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas, with weekend observed-day shifts) instead of an external market-calendar library.
assumptions.reason: Only backtrader/math/collections/statistics imports are permitted, so pandas_market_calendars-style libraries are unavailable; an algorithmic calendar correctly generalizes to arbitrary past/future dates as the spec requires.

assumptions.choice: Treat early-close sessions (e.g., day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve) as ordinary business days, not holidays.
assumptions.reason: The filter concerns days the exchange is fully closed; early closes are still open trading days, so excluding them would be an unstated addition.

assumptions.choice: Only force-close a position if it was opened (filled) on the same calendar day that is the last business day of that week; positions opened earlier in the week and still held are not force-closed by this rule.
assumptions.reason: Literal spec wording is 'if a position is opened on the last business day of the week, it must be forcibly closed at the end of that day' -- a same-day condition, not a general end-of-week flatten of all open positions.

assumptions.choice: Treat a position as 'opened' on the bar its buy order is actually filled (backtrader's default next-bar-open execution), not the bar the entry signal was generated on.
assumptions.reason: Backtrader fills market orders at the next bar's open by default; notify_order reports the actual fill bar, which is the natural reading of 'opened'.

assumptions.choice: Evaluate exit/close signals every bar regardless of business-day status, per the explicit 'Conditions for exiting a position' section.
assumptions.reason: That section states exits execute on any day, while the later 'risk management' section says rule activation is business-day only -- a direct contradiction; since the AAPL feed only contains bars on actual trading days, both readings are behaviorally identical, so the more specific exit-conditions wording was followed.

assumptions.choice: Skip signal evaluation until at least 2 bars are available (len(self) >= 2).
assumptions.reason: The chosen placeholder entry/exit rule compares close[0] to close[-1] and needs one prior bar to avoid an out-of-range reference; this is bounds safety for the assumed signal, not indicator warm-up.
